source_scope: Norfolk County, Virginia, Deed Book 9 (1710–1717), pp. 348–350; Daniel Glasgow to Thomas Miller, lease 15 September and release 16 September 1714, acknowledged 17 September 1714; FamilySearch DGS 007645618, images 523–525.
source_reading: A second original transaction identifies Daniel Glasgow as a planter of Moyock, Albemarle County, North Carolina. By a lease dated 15 September 1714 and release dated 16 September, he conveyed 100 acres to Thomas Miller. The release names Daniel senior; Mary joined it and acknowledged her consent in court on 17 September. Daniel Glasgow junior witnessed both instruments with John Nicholls and G. Halliday. The deeds recite Thomas Miller’s 800-acre patent of 20 April 1689 and his conveyance of this 100-acre parcel to Daniel on 16 May 1692, acknowledged on 17 May. Thus this 1714 original supplies a specific 1692 acquisition to follow; the original 1692 deed was located and inspected on 30 October 2026, completing this acquisition test.
limitations: The 100-acre Miller parcel is distinct from the 80 acres inherited through John Gamon and from the 100-acre Henry Slade parcel sold in 1729. Shared acreage alone does not join those titles. The same court day, Moyock residence, Mary, Daniel junior and John Nicholls strongly identify the senior as the father in the separately proved Gamon deed. This adds chronology and a witness network, without naming William Glasgow-428 as a son or resolving junior’s later identity. Father ratings remain junior→Glasgow-3322 98%, William-428→Daniel-1158 42%, Daniel-1158→Robert-1157 12%, and Daniel-3322→Robert-1157 34%.
next_test: Trace the Richford 80-acre tract after1714 for junior’s wife, heirs or later residence; independently seek a named-kin or title bridge from Daniel senior to Robert. The1692acquisition test is complete; do not redispatch it or search only the superseded Willson reading.

follow_up_20261030.body: The original conveyance of 16 May 1692, acknowledged in Norfolk court on 17 May, names Daniel Glascock of Norfolk County as purchaser of 100 acres from Thomas Miller and Elizabeth his wife. It identifies Miller’s 800-acre patent of 20 April 1689 and land on the Northwest River between the two Indian Creeks. The inspected 1714 lease repeats that patent, acreage, deed date, acknowledgment and particular land description for Daniel Glasgow’s earlier acquisition. These linked title particulars identify the 1692 Glascock purchaser with the 1714 Glasgow senior, rather than relying on surname resemblance alone. Reinspection of the 1714 original also confirms Thomas Miller: the earlier Willson reading is corrected.
follow_up_20261030.limits: Elizabeth is Miller’s wife, not Daniel’s. The 1692 deed names neither Daniel’s father nor a wife or son of Daniel. It does not connect the separate Gamon 80-acre tract or Slade 100-acre tract, identify junior’s later family, establish Scottish origin or resolve whether Glasgow-1158 duplicates the senior account Glasgow-3322. Existing father ratings and all vital fields remain unchanged.
